history.recommendation_text: 7. The Board recommends that the Department of Management and the Department of Field Support settle receivables from United Nations related party entities within 12 months.
history.reference_raw: A/71/5 (Vol. II), chap. II, for the; para. 48
history.administration_response: The Administration’s comments are reflected in paragraph 49 of A/71/5 (Vol. II), chap. II. In addition, the Department of Management has recently implemented a “monthly assurance and monitoring dashboard” for the early detection and timely follow-up of delayed processing of various transactions, including long-outstanding receivables. The Department of Management will also update the monthly closing checklist of field missions with respect to long- outstanding receivables from United Nations-related entities in particular. There was an improvement in 2016/17. Receivables more than one year old were $144.7 million as at 30 June 2016, and they decreased to $142.8 million as at 30 June 2017. Of those balances, $131.5 million is due from Member States and is not expected to be settled in the foreseeable future. The net receivables of the $131.5 million were $13.2 million and $11.3 million. The decrease was 14 per cent, which was not impressive but notable. The Administration will intensify its efforts to further reduce the long-outstanding receivables in financial year 2017/18.

history.reference_raw: A/71/5 (Vol. II), chap. II, for the year ended 30 June 2016; para. 48
history.administration_response: The Office of Programme Planning, Budget and Accounts (now the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget) stated that the receivables from other United Nations entities became more visible through the implementation of a separate cost recovery fund. Previously, they had been commingled with various receivables in the mission accounts. The overdue receivables are also flagged in the monthly monitoring dashboard for the attention of the missions and their prompt follow-up. The target date for implementation is the second quarter of 2018.

history.recommendation_text: In paragraph 48 of its report, the Board recommended that the Department of Management and the Department of Field Support settle receivables from United Nations related party entities within 12 months.
history.reference_raw: Recommendations conta ined in the report of the Board of Auditors for the 12 -month period ended 30 June 2016 ( A/71/5 (Vol. II)
history.entities_raw: All peacekeeping missions, Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance and Department of Operational Support
history.sg_progress: The Administration is increasing its efforts to ensure the settlement of receivables due from United Nations related party entities within the recommended period of 12 months. Some examples include the following: (a) UNMISS, in collaboration with the Regional Service Centre in Entebbe, Uganda, is making efforts to ensure the settlement of receivables due from United Nations related party entities within the stipulated 12-month period; (b) UNISFA is making efforts to settle all receivables within the specified time frame. In addition, the Force is revising its memorandums of understanding with agencies to ensure that services rendered by the Force are paid in advance, thus minimizing the number and amount of receivables; (c) MONUSCO wishes to clarify that most of its related parties have deployed Umoja and that therefore the Mission is using the sales and distribution module for cost recovery. For the related parties that are not using Umoja, sales orders are raised and the Mission has dedicated finance personnel to follow outstanding receivables that are more than a month old. The finance personnel even visit clients to speed up the recovery and, if necessary, they escalate issues to the Mission’s management. B. Recommendations contained in the report of the Board of Auditors for the 12-month period ended 30 June 2017 (A/72/5 (Vol. II), chap. II)
